items.title: Chinese Hackers Use AI-Powered ARTEX to Target Over 200 Organizations Worldwide
items.reason: Nation-state actor (Vapor Panda/China) ran an AI-orchestrated pentesting framework (ARTEX) with planner/worker LLM agents across 200+ orgs, confirmed by CrowdStrike and Zscaler with concrete technical chain details.

CrowdStrike: one intrusion's planning agents consumed ~1.4B input tokens.
Starting Oct 17, 2026: 200+ orgs targeted, post-exploitation confirmed at 9 (BLOODALCHEMY/ShadowPad derivative deployed), credential scanning at 12+ more.
Targets: foreign ministries across 4 continents, 19 US orgs, telecoms in US/Belgium/Philippines.
Chained technique: unsigned SAML assertion + XXE to reach cloud instance metadata, LAPS reads, RBCD, forged admin tokens via keys unrotated since 2022, reused leaked 2024 VPN config/client key.
Sources: CrowdStrike ('Vapor Panda uses ARTEX...'), Zscaler ThreatLabz, WSJ report on the developer.

items.title: Malware uses LLMs to rank victims by how much they're worth
items.reason: Cisco Talos documents real infostealer malware (VOLTA-AUTODOXER) that sends a built dossier of stolen victim data to an LLM (via OpenRouter) which scores victims' monetizable value and OPSEC, with a model fallback chain to dodge refusals - concrete AI-as-analyst mechanism, primary source.
key_facts: Pipeline: steal (browser creds, cookies, cards, crypto wallets, SSH/cloud keys, Wi-Fi) -> enrich (Gmail receipts, food-delivery history, Roblox inventory lookup) -> build Identity_Report.txt dossier -> send as JSON to OpenRouter -> get AI_Analysis.txt ranking 'WHAT THEY'RE WORTH' and 'THEIR OPSEC' -> exfiltrate both zipped.
Default model anthropic/claude-opus-4.6, fallback chain moonshotai/kimi-k2 then google/gemini-2.5-flash, temperature 0.2; malware detects refusal phrases and advances the chain.
Talos frames this as 'effort displacement': an LLM replaces the operator's manual triage/analysis step, not code generation or evasion.
Reported by Cisco Talos (author Ryan Fetterman) via its CAIRN research effort.

items.title: TCP Use-After-Free: CVE-2026-98432 / CVSS 9.8
items.reason: CVSS 9.8 remote unauthenticated Linux TCP use-after-free; Anthropic reports Claude wrote a working remote-root exploit after prompting, landmark AI-exploit-dev story with primary source and technical detail.
key_facts: Use-after-free in Linux IPv4 TCP handshake option handling; race lets a freed request-socket options struct be read by another CPU.
Upstream fix (Dumazet, commit e3f33b0) swaps two kfree() for kfree_rcu().
Anthropic's unpublished PoC gets root command execution on MPTCP listener hosts in ~48 min to leak a kernel pointer plus ~5 more min to RCE; reported via Anthropic researcher Xinyang Ge.
Go opens MPTCP listeners by default since Go 1.24, widening exposure.
Fixed upstream Oct 11-18, 2026; distro coverage uneven (Debian/SUSE/Oracle UEK/Amazon Linux fixed; Ubuntu/RHEL not yet; AlmaLinux in testing); not in CISA KEV as of report.
36 GitHub repos referenced the CVE by Oct 31, at least 6 claiming a PoC (unverified by author).

items.title: Memdoor: A team of 5 Qwen3.8-27B models beats Fable 5 on LiveCodeBench Hard
items.reason: Multi-agent decomposition (5x Qwen3.8-27B via Memdoor) matches/beats a larger frontier model on LiveCodeBench Hard with running code and transparent numbers/caveats - concrete eval-methodology result, not just a benchmark claim.
key_facts: Memdoor team-solve: 5 file-communicating roles (planner, 2 ideators, solver, manager) + repair worker, each fresh-context; shell-script test harness decides success, one repair round, no human gate.
5-pass avg on first 10 LiveCodeBench Hard problems: Memdoor 9.8/10 vs authors' own harness 9.6/10 vs Fable 5 alone 8.0/10.
50 runs: 49 solved; total cost $35.79; median run $0.39 / 40 minutes.
Author-noted caveats: only 10 problems, possible training-data contamination, Fable 5 baseline not rerun in this harness, used OpenRouter not authors' own FP8 vLLM setup.
